title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Notation. A and B are small categories. A^ = Hom(A°, Ens) is the category of presheaves on A. A^∨ = Hom(A, Ens) = (A°)^ is the category of copresheaves. Hom^! means functors commuting with projective limits; Hom_! means functors commuting with inductive limits. The page continues the previous one, which treats 'functorial correspondences' (profunctors/distributors) and a circle/hexagon of equivalent descriptions.

(1) Upper-left margin: the case B = A°. The Hom functor gives a canonical element H_A ∈ (A×A°)^. Its two curryings are the Yoneda embeddings A → A^ and A° → A^∨. Each extends uniquely in two ways:
- by limit-preserving functors A^{∨°} → A^ and A^{^°} → A^∨, which are the two halves of Isbell conjugation;
- by colimit-preserving functors, which are the identities A^ → A^ and A^∨ → A^∨.
Together these give a canonical bifunctor A^{^°} × A^{∨°} → Ens, limit-preserving in each variable: (X,Y) ↦ Hom(X, Spec Y) = Hom(Y, O X). The margin also records the self-duality statements:
- A^ ≃ Hom^!(A^{^°}, Ens): every limit-preserving presheaf on A^ is representable.
- A^ ≃ Hom_!(A^∨, Ens): A^∨ is the free cocompletion of A°.
- Dually for A^∨.
These are the standard universal properties of free (co)completions.

(2) Main diagram: the many faces of a distributor X ∈ (A×B)^.
(A×B)^ ≃ Hom(B°, A^) ≃ Hom(A°, B^)
≃ Hom_!(B^∨, A^) ≃ Hom^!(B^{^°}, A^)
≃ Hom^!(A^{^°}, B^) ≃ Hom_!(A^∨, B^)
≃ Hom_!!(A^∨ × B^∨, Ens) (bicocontinuous)
≃ Hom^!!(A^{^°} × B^{^°}, Ens) =: Bifais(A^, B^), the 'bisheaves' (functors limit-preserving in each variable).
In modern terms: Psh(A) ⊗ Psh(B) ≃ Psh(A×B), and profunctors ≃ cocontinuous functors between presheaf categories. The last form, Bifais, describes the tensor product dually, via continuous functors on the opposite categories.

(3) Relative formalism. Write p_B: A×B → A and p_A: A×B → B for the projections, and q: A, B → e. Define relative internal Homs:
- Hom_A(X,Y) := p_{B*} Hom_{A×B}(X,Y), a presheaf on A;
- Hom_B(X,Y) := p_{A*} Hom_{A×B}(X,Y), a presheaf on B.
Global sections are compatible: Γ_{A×B} = Γ_A ∘ p_{B*}.

For X ∈ (A×B)^ he defines the two integral transforms ('kernels'):
- ^sX(L) = p_{A*} Hom(p_B^*L, X) ∈ B^, for L ∈ A^;
- ^dX(M) = p_{B*} Hom(p_A^*M, X) ∈ A^, for M ∈ B^.
The 'bisheaf' X(L,M) = Hom(L⊠M, X), with L⊠M = p_B^*L × p_A^*M, satisfies
X(L,M) ≅ Hom_{A^}(L, ^dX(M)) ≅ Hom_{B^}(M, ^sX(L)),
by the adjunctions p^* ⊣ p_*. This is exactly what shows that X(-,-) is limit-preserving in each variable, i.e. that X defines an object of Bifais(A^,B^).

He then checks the following. Let X define B° → A^, b ↦ ^dX(b). Compose it with the representable functor Hom(L_0, -): A^ → Ens. The result b ↦ Hom(L_0, ^dX(b)) is the presheaf ^sX(L_0). So L_0 ↦ ^sX(L_0) is the limit-preserving extension of A° → B^. This makes the 'arrows ≈' of the diagram explicit.

(4) Last third. He claims:
- (L,M) ↦ L⊠M, A^×B^ → (A×B)^, is fully faithful;
- composed with (A×B)^ ≃ Hom^!!(A^{^°}×B^{^°}, Ens) ⊂ (A^×B^)^, it is the Yoneda functor of A^×B^;
- Hom(L'⊠M', L''⊠M'') ≅ Hom(L',L'') × Hom(M',M''), with an internal analogue;
- hence Hom_{A×B}(p_A^*M, p_B^*L) ≅ p_B^*L, i.e. (p_B^*L)^M ≅ p_B^*L, where X^M := Hom(p_A^*M, X).
The page breaks off at '⊢'. The next sheet is a computer banner dated 2 June 1982, which gives a terminus post quem.
errors: The claim that ⊠: A^×B^ → (A×B)^ is fully faithful is false in general. Take A = B = e: ⊠ is then the product Ens×Ens → Ens. Already Hom(2×2, 2×2) has 256 elements, while Hom(2,2)×Hom(2,2) has 16. Objects (L,∅) all go to ∅. The functor is bicocontinuous (it is the universal bicocontinuous functor, the tensor product), but not fully faithful.

Consequently the formula Hom(L'⊠M', L''⊠M'') ≅ Hom(L',L'')×Hom(M',M'') is wrong. The correct computation is Hom(L'⊠M', p_B^*L'') = Hom(L' × const(colim M'), L'') = Hom(colim M', Hom(L',L'')). This agrees with Hom(L',L'') only when colim M' = 1, for instance M' representable.

Likewise the internal formula Hom_{A×B}(L'⊠M', L''⊠M'') ≅ Hom(L',L'')⊠Hom(M',M'') is wrong. So are its special cases Hom(p_A^*M, p_B^*L) ≅ p_B^*L and (p_B^*L)^M ≅ p_B^*L. In the point case these say L^M ≅ L.

The claim that the composite with the inclusion into (A^×B^)^ is the Yoneda functor of A^×B^ is also false. The bisheaf of L⊠M is (L1,M1) ↦ Hom(L1⊠M1, L⊠M), not Hom(L1,L)×Hom(M1,M). These statements hold only after restricting to representables a, b (or 'connected' objects).
Slip in the margin: 'b ↦ ^dX(b) = Hom_B(p_B^*(L),X)'. This should read ^dX(b) = Hom_A(p_A^*b, X); the formula written is the one for ^sX(L).
The final '⊢' and the absence of continuation suggest the thread (or its error) was abandoned or corrected on a lost or other sheet.

ideas.what: Isbell conjugation between presheaves A^ and copresheaves A^∨, obtained as limit-preserving extensions of the two Yoneda embeddings via the canonical element H_A ∈ (A×A°)^
A^ ≃ continuous functors (A^)^op → Ens ≃ cocontinuous functors A^∨ → Ens (self-duality via free completions)
ideas.modern_name: universal properties of free cocompletion / free completion; representability of continuous presheaves on a presheaf topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory 1982; SGA4 Exp. I for the colimit side)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I (extension of functors along Yoneda, colimit side)

ideas.what: Equivalent descriptions of a distributor X ∈ (A×B)^: functors B°→A^, cocontinuous A^∨→B^, continuous (A^)^op→B^, bicocontinuous A^∨×B^∨→Ens, bicontinuous (A^)^op×(B^)^op→Ens ('Bifais(A^,B^)')
ideas.modern_name: profunctors ≃ cocontinuous functors between presheaf categories (Eilenberg–Watts for presheaves); Psh(A)⊗Psh(B) ≃ Psh(A×B); tensor product of locally presentable categories as continuous functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou (distributeurs, 1967/73), Lawvere; Kelly; Pitts (1985) for products of toposes as tensor products

ideas.what: Relative internal Homs Hom_A = p_{B*}Hom_{A×B} and the two integral transforms ^sX, ^dX with the adjunction formula X(L,M) = Hom(L⊠M,X) ≅ Hom(L, ^dX(M)) ≅ Hom(M, ^sX(L))
ideas.modern_name: integral transforms with kernel / Fourier–Mukai-style formalism for presheaf toposes; external product ⊠
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard topos theory (SGA4 external products); integral-transform viewpoint e.g. Ben-Zvi–Francis–Nadler, Lurie in higher setting

ideas.what: Attempted full faithfulness of ⊠: A^×B^ → (A×B)^ and identification with Yoneda of A^×B^
ideas.modern_name: (false) — correct statement: ⊠ is the universal bicocontinuous functor

missed.claim: Historical: in mid-1982 Grothendieck was working out, for presheaf toposes, the description of the product topos (A×B)^ both as bicocontinuous and as bicontinuous functors ('Bifais'). This anticipates in a special case Pitts' 1985 description of products of toposes as tensor products of cocomplete categories, under the heading 'dualité des topos'. Mathematically it is now standard; the interest is only documentary.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's independent, then-unpublished engagement with the bicategory of distributors and Isbell-type duality between A^ and A^∨ around the time of Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful but standard working-out of profunctors, Isbell conjugation and the tensor product of presheaf toposes, all in the literature (Bénabou, Isbell, Kelly, Pitts). The only notable features are the 'Bifais' terminology, the dating (June 1982 or later), and a genuine error (claimed full faithfulness of ⊠ and the formula (p_B^*L)^M ≅ p_B^*L) at the point where the page breaks off.
transcription_corrections: Margin line: 'i.e. faisceaux sur A^∨ resp. A^, ind. de [?] A^ resp. A^∨' more plausibly reads 'i.e. faisceaux sur A^∨ resp. A^ à val. ds A^ resp. A^∨' (sheaves with values in).

Right-hand bottom of the main diagram: the 'Hom' before '_{!!}(A^∨×B^∨,(Ens))' is struck and rewritten. The bracketed copy at the left, [Hom_{!!}(A^∨×B^∨,(Ens))], sits under Hom_!(B^∨,A^) behind the diagonal line separating the marginal B = A° discussion.
'^dX(b)=Hom_B(p_B^*(L),X)' is faithfully transcribed, but it is Grothendieck's slip for Hom_A(p_A^*b, X).
Top centre: page number '(1)' circled; bottom-left: archive page number '3'.
